end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels from farm to plate.
Identified that farther food usually uses more fuel and produces more smoke.
Compared local and distant foods using distance, freshness, refrigeration, and packaging.
Recognised that the 10 km option travels less and is likely fresher; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles and comparing foods by travel distance, fuel use, pollution, freshness, refrigeration, and packaging. They used the method of linking a longer journey with more fuel and smoke, and connected shorter journeys with freshness. Rohan initially needed clarification about the word “farmer”; this was corrected through later comparisons. At home, ask them to compare two foods by writing their likely source, distance, fuel use, and freshness.
